perAttempt.design_summary: Claude's reply parks the submarine on columns 5–6 and makes fire the default action (fire logit 0, every other action −13 or lower when no layer-2 unit is on). Layer 1 is almost entirely "row-gated" units: each gets 15 per sub cell in its row against a bias of about −30, so only the unit for the sub's current row is off saturation. There are four groups: 9 vertical-urge units V0–V8, which weigh targets in other rows by distance (ch2 counts +, ch1 counts −½) and push away from danger in adjacent rows; 7 turn units T2–T8, whose pre-activation is ±0.4 for facing plus 0.4·(ch1+ch2 in cols 7–9 minus cols 0–3); 7 own-row hold/dodge units E2–E8, computed as tanh(6·ch2 − 4.5·ch1 + 3·adjacent danger); and singles R01, SURF (oxygen<60 AND ≥1 diver), XR and XL (column-sum centering). Layer 2 builds DOWN (6v − 6e − 1.8), UP (−6v − 6e − 1.8, +30 under SURF), TURN-R/TURN-L (on when the T pre-activation is beyond ±1.0) and two centering units gated off while holding. Each layer-2 unit adds about ±12 to its action's logit; centering adds ±8. The intended behaviour: track rows with divers or enemies, hold a row that has a target, turn to face it and fire, dodge bullets, rest at rows 4–5, never press up in rows 0–1 unless surfacing, and surface when oxygen is low with a diver aboard. Probes confirm almost every stated threshold. The failures come from the turn detector, which reads absolute columns and the shared trail channel, and from a surfacing climb that ignores danger.

units.computes: Row-gated vertical urge (+ = down): ch2 targets in other rows weighted 2/1.6/1.2/0.9/0.7/0.6 by distance, ch1 at −half (diver +w, enemy +w/2, bullet −w/2), adjacent-row danger in cols 3-8 repels (2.5), rows 0-1 never attract; bias gives resting depth rows 4-5; V0/V1 baseline +2 (dive) minus 1.9 per danger cell in the row below.

units.computes: Turn signal pre-activation = ±0.4 facing (+ = facing left, from ch0 weights 15.4/15/14.6/14.2 and ch4 weights −0.8/0.8/1.6 at cols 4/6/7) + 0.4·(ch1+ch2 in cols 7-9 − cols 0-3). Enemy = 0.8, diver or bullet = 0.4.

units.computes: Own-row status tanh(6·ch2 − 4.5·ch1 + 3·danger in adjacent rows cols 3-8): enemy +0.91, diver +1.0 (hold), bullet −1.0 (dodge), empty 0.
units.evidence: probe_claude.py: own-row fish E=+0.91, diver E=+1.00, bullet E=−1.00 -> up/down 0.5/0.5; fish row5 col4 adjacent E=+1.00 -> fire (hold).

units.computes: R01 = tanh(0)=0 in rows 0-1, −1 elsewhere. SURF = tanh(6·in[593] − 6·in[557] − 3): on only when diver gauge col8 lit and oxygen col2 dark (oxygen<60, ≥1 diver). XR/XL = column-weighted ch0 sum: ±0.91 at cells 5-6, flip to +0.91 when the sub drifts to 6-7 or 4-5.

units.computes: DOWN = 6v − 6e − 1.8 in rows 2-8 (6v − 1.8 in rows 0-1, −20 under SURF). UP = −6v − 6e − 1.8 in rows 2-8, at least +16 under SURF regardless of danger. In rows 0-1 UP = −6v − 13.8 (blocked), or −6v + 16.2 under SURF.

units.computes: 40·t − 30.46 (TURN-L also gets −100·R01 + bias): on when the T pre-activation is above +1.0 (or below −1.0). It does not check whether the sub already faces that way, so it can shift the sub.

units.computes: 4·XR − 4e − 2 (and the mirror with XL): steers back to cols 5-6 only while the own-row E unit is ≤ ~0, so it is suppressed while an enemy or diver is in the row.

implementation_bugs.description: The facing reading in the T units uses ch4 (trail OR sub_back) at cols 4/6/7 with weights −0.8/+0.8/+1.6, so enemy and diver trails are read as the sub's back cell. A single foreign trail at col 7 (+1.6) by itself exceeds the +1.0 TURN threshold, so the sub presses right whatever its facing. The reply says facing 'is read from the back cell (ch4)'; the weights read any trail.
implementation_bugs.evidence: probe2.py: 'facing R (cells5-6), lone foreign trail at col7' Tpre=+1.20 -> right p=1.0; 'diver col8 moving R (trail col7)' Tpre=+1.60 -> right. shifts.py over 200 episodes: 250 of 707 TURN- or sticky-driven shifts (rows ≥2) had a foreign trail in cols 4/6/7. The thinking flagged the risk ('its trail would push the turn units toward turning right, which could lead me straight into it') but did not fix it.
implementation_bugs.estimated_effect: Accounts for a large share of the 3.74 unintended shifts per episode. It contributes to the 39 of 200 deaths where a left/right press shifted the sub into an enemy. No isolated counterfactual was run.

implementation_bugs.description: The T units and the facing window are fixed in absolute columns (sides = cols 0-3 vs 7-9, facing calibrated for cells 4-7). When the sub drifts off cols 5-6, facing is read with the wrong sign, and an enemy at col 7 behind a sub on cols 8-9 counts as 'right'. Centering is gated off while anything is in the row, so the sub cannot return. The reply says it 'never steers horizontally except to turn'.
implementation_bugs.evidence: probe2.py: cells 7-8 facing L gives Tpre=−0.80 (reads as facing right); cells 8-9 facing R with a fish at col 7 behind gives TURN_R=+1.00, CL=−0.92 -> right. replay.py seed 2 t=508-516: the sub pressed right at col 9 for 9 steps until the fish hit it. colstats.py: 748 shifts in 200 episodes (3.74/ep); front column outside 5-6 in 9.5% of row≥2 steps. shifts.py: 261 of the 707 shifts began off-center. Three unclassified deaths (seeds 39, 78, 118) were enemies spawning onto a sub parked at col 9.
implementation_bugs.estimated_effect: Part of the 83 deaths on left/right presses (41.5% of episodes). Not isolated by a counterfactual.

implementation_bugs.description: Divers count in the turn sum, because ch2 is weighted equally with ch1: a diver is 0.4, an enemy 0.8, and facing gives only ±0.4 against a ±1.0 threshold. So one diver on the side the sub faces cancels an enemy approaching from behind (0.4 + 0.8 − 0.4 = 0.8 < 1.0), and the sub keeps firing away from the enemy. This contradicts the reply's 'It turns to face the enemy and fires.' Col 4 is also in neither side window, so an enemy at col 4 behind a right-facing sub gives Tpre=−0.4 and no turn.
implementation_bugs.evidence: probe2.py: 'facing L, fish col9 + diver col2' Tpre=+0.80 -> fire; 'facing R, fish col4 moving R' Tpre=−0.40 -> fire. missed_turns.py: of 919 steps with an approaching enemy behind a centred sub and no enemy ahead, the turn unit was off in 349; 342 of those (37.2% of all 919) had a diver on the facing side. late_turn.py: seeds 6, 21, 31 show 7+ steps facing a diver while a fish closes from behind, then a late turn onto it.
implementation_bugs.estimated_effect: Unproven score cost. Zeroing ch2 in the T units and doubling ch1 (nodiverT) scored 7.06±0.49 vs 8.03±0.54 baseline on seeds 0-199, so this edit gave no measurable gain.

perAttempt.why_this_score: The policy does most of what the reply says. Diving, resting depth, diver tracking, the row-1 guard and oxygen surfacing all check out in probes and in play (0 oxygen deaths, 6.7 pickups per episode). Episodes are short, though: the mean length is 350 steps on seeds 0-199 (327.6 on the official 1,000), about 2.85 deaths per 1,000 steps. The kill rate is 2.09 per 100 steps, so the score is about 7.3 kills plus a 0.7 surfacing bonus (8.03±0.54 on seeds 0-199; 7.41 on 1,000). Deaths spread across three mechanisms: (a) the danger-blind surfacing climb, 33% of episodes; (b) the leaky turn detector producing late turns and shifts into enemies, 41.5%; (c) sticky vertical moves, about 14%. Removing one barely moves the score. An oracle safe-surface wrapper gives 10.9, and a diver-free turn sum gives 7.1, which is not significant. Turning is load-bearing: forcing left and right off (b3[1]=b3[3]=−100) drops the score to 2.36, because the hold logic then parks the sub in rows with enemies arriving from behind. The score sits above the zero floor (0.1) and PPO 100M (5.6) because the vertical, diver and oxygen logic is sound, and far below Astra because the sub survives only about 350 steps.
perAttempt.vs_astra: Astra's net, probed the same way, never presses left or right (b3 left/right = −100; 0 left/right executions in 200 episodes) and always faces left at col 5. Its layer 1 has: 9 row indicators; 7 diver-row detectors (8·ch2 − 8·ch1, so enemies cancel); 8 hazard detectors near the sub's column (ch1 weight 7 at cols 4-6, enemies partly cancelled by ch2, so bullets weigh more); 1 surface request; and 7 left-side shooting-opportunity detectors. Layer 2 has 24 'candidate row' units (stay/up/down per row), each scoring diver and shooting attraction minus a hazard penalty, read out with gain 30 as an argmax. Probes: an own-row fish at col 4, 6 or 7, or a bullet, gives a 50/50 up/down dodge; a fish at col 1 gives fire; a shootable fish two rows down draws the sub down (p=.85); a fish directly above during surfacing makes it wait (fire .86). In play (seeds 0-199): 53.71±2.99, 1,432 steps per episode, 0.70 deaths per 1,000 steps, 3.33 kills per 100 steps, 9 surfacings and 30 pickups per episode, and 6.0 points of six-diver bonus. Astra's surfacing requests succeed about 96.5% of the time (Claude's about 78%), and its surfacing deaths are almost all sticky repeats (68 of 72). Only 23 of 180 collisions happen in its own row (Claude: 98 of 192); 157 are vertical moves, 119 of them sticky. The two designs collect divers at about the same rate (2.1 vs 1.9 per 100 steps). The gap is mostly survival: about 4.1× longer episodes, then 1.6× kill rate, then the bonus that only long episodes reach. Astra handles approaching enemies with a one-step vertical dodge and never relies on horizontal logic. Claude's design holds rows and turns to fight, so it depends on a turn detector that the linear readout of trails, divers and absolute columns makes unreliable, and its surfacing climb has no hazard term. That difference accounts for the 7.4 vs 53.1 gap.

perAttempt.design_summary: Claude built a turret that tries to stay in the centre columns (4-5), turns to face an enemy in its own row and fires, and moves up or down toward rows that hold targets. The first layer has 4 groups of 7 units, one unit per player row 2-8 (weight 10 on each player cell, bias -20, so only the active row's unit is off -1). The groups are V (vertical pull toward rewards, plus a ±4 danger veto on the adjacent row in columns 2-7), O (facing direction, read from the player and trail channels in columns 3-6 only), D (side of the target in absolute columns: 0-3 count negative, 6-9 positive, enemies weigh ±1.2, divers and bullets ±0.6, plus a small re-centre term) and Y (enemy bullet in my row, danger minus reward). Two more units are global: S (oxygen below 60 and at least one diver, read from gauge cells (9,2) and (9,8)) and R01 (player in row 0 or 1). Layer 2 sums each group, which gives an affine function of the active unit, and thresholds it into 16 conditions: up-desire, down-veto, down-desire, up-veto, fire-right/left, turn-right/left, step-right/left, dodge-up/down, plus copies of S and R01 and their two ANDs. The logits form a priority table: dodge 10, leave rows 0/1 10, surface 9, fire or turn 7, vertical chase 3, step/re-centre 1.5, default fire 1, no-op 0, vetoed move -11 to -26. Divers are chased like targets, both vertically (V) and horizontally (the D step unit).

units.computes: Gated vertical drive. A target in another row pulls the sub toward it (0.5, 0.4, 0.3... by distance). Danger in columns 2-7 of the row above or below gives ±4, pushing V into the band |V|>0.9, which acts as a veto. V_2 has an extra -0.5 bias and ignores row 1.

In play, inactive per-row units never differ from -1 by more than 1.19e-7 (drift.py).

units.computes: Facing direction, as 2*(front-back) from channel-0 weights 2c+1 and channel-4 weights 18-4c, but only in columns 3-6. Outside that window the channel-0 weight is 10 and the channel-4 weight is 0.

units.computes: Signed side of the target in absolute columns: columns 0-3 count -0.6, 6-9 count +0.6, and 4-5 count 0, for both danger and reward. An enemy gives ±1.2 (tanh ≈ ±0.83), a diver or bullet ±0.6 (±0.537). A re-centre term adds ±0.06 per column of drift.

units.computes: Enemy bullet in my row: 3*(danger) - 3*(reward) over the whole row, bias -21.5. An enemy cancels itself and a diver subtracts.
units.evidence: probe2.py: bullet in row gives Y=+0.905 and up/down 0.50/0.50. Bullet plus a diver in the same row gives Y=-0.905 and no dodge (fire 0.73, noop 0.27).

units.computes: S = gauge(9,8) on AND gauge(9,2) off, meaning oxygen <60 and at least one diver. R01 = player in row 0 or 1.
units.evidence: probe2.py: row 5, oxygen 50, 1 diver gives S=+0.99 and up p=1.00; 0 divers gives S=-0.99; oxygen 70 with 3 divers gives no surfacing. probe1.py: start state (row 0) gives R01=+1 and down p=1.00.

units.computes: Thresholds on the active V: up-desire (80V-4.8>0, V>0.06), down-veto (40V-36>0, V>0.9), down-desire (V<-0.06), up-veto (V<-0.9). The up logit gets 4.5*(upDes-dnVeto), so it is +9 only for 0.06<V<0.9.
units.evidence: b2 values in answer.md lines 206-213. probe2.py shows chase logit +3.00 and veto logit -25.99.

units.computes: fireR/fireL/turnR/turnL = ±100D ± 40O - 110 (an enemy on the side AND facing it, or facing away). stepR/stepL = ±60D - 3.6, true for any |D|>0.06.

units.computes: dodgeUp (80V+100Y-75.2) and dodgeDn (-80V+100Y-84.8), both on when |V| is small, so the dodge is 50/50. Then copies of S and R01, surf1 = S AND R01 (up 11 from row 1), and leave01 = R01 AND NOT S (down 10).

implementation_bugs.description: The orientation read O_k is only valid while both sub cells lie in columns 3-6. One column outside, the sign is inverted. Two or more columns outside, it is 0. The reply states flatly that O 'equals 2·(front − back)'. Inside the window, enemy trails also corrupt it: a fish moving away leaves its trail on the sub's cell and drives O to 0. The window was a deliberate trade-off, and my full-width linear version did much worse (1.18), but the off-window failure is not acknowledged.

In play (summarize.py), O is wrong-sign on 6.7% and near zero on 4.9% of row 2-8 steps, but at the fatal step of 181 collisions it was wrong 62 times and zero 69 times (classify.py).

The sub then walks toward the enemy, although the reply describes this path only as 're-centre or step toward a diver'.

implementation_bugs.description: Horizontal steering toward divers overrides re-centring, and D uses absolute columns, not columns relative to the sub. The reply says the sub 'keeps near the centre columns (4–5)', but a diver weighs ±0.6 against 0.06 per column of drift, so the sub follows divers to the walls. Enemies spawn at the walls, and the O, D and veto windows all assume a centred sub. A diver at col 6 still reads as 'right' when the sub is at col 8.

perAttempt.why_this_score:
Score = points per step × survival. On seeds 0-199 (mean 8.34, se 0.64, against 7.451 over 1,000 episodes in run.json), Claude earns 0.0276 points per step (7.92 kills + 0.42 bonus per episode) and survives 302 steps (median 201). perAttempt.design_summary:
The submarine dives from the surface, moves right to column 9 and steps left once, so it sits at column 8 facing left. After that it moves only up and down, firing left by default. Fire has logit 10; a chosen up, down, left or right move has logit 20 to 22, so the policy is almost deterministic (sampled actions over 200 episodes: fire 81.3%, up 9.0%, down 9.3%). Layer 1 holds 29 feature units:
- 9 sub-row indicators (S_r).
- 8 row-attraction scores (R_r). These combine a column-weighted reward channel with a negative trail term, so objects coming toward column 8 score higher than ones moving away.
- 8 row-danger flags (U_r): any danger cell in columns 6–9 of a row.
- A 'certainly has a diver' gauge test (HD) and a 'time to surface' gauge test (SURF).
- Two units for horizontal homing (HR, HL).
Layer 2 gates each move with the current row's S_r: 8 Up_r units, 8 Down_r units, two relays for horizontal homing, and a BLOCK unit that stops surfacing from row 1 without a confirmed diver. Each Up_r/Down_r unit adds danger in the current row (+50), SURF (+50 up, -30 down) and distance-weighted attraction (8, 5, 3.5, 2.5, 2; downward ×1.25). It subtracts 150 when the destination row's danger flag is on. The design only checks the next row. It has no protection against a sticky action repeating a vertical move into the row beyond, and that gap causes most deaths.

perAttempt.why_this_score:
The score is kills plus surfacing bonus: 45.95 + 3.88 = 49.83 per episode on seeds 0-199, against 51.69 ± 1.36 over 1,000 episodes. No episode reaches the 10,000-step cap. Every episode ends in death after a mean of 1,241 steps, and the sub kills 3.70 enemies per 100 steps. The weights carry out the reply's design faithfully: every hand-built probe produced the action the design calls for. What limits the score is lifetime:
- 66% of deaths come from a sticky action repeating a vertical move into a row the policy had correctly flagged as dangerous. The design checks only one row ahead.
- 17.5% are oxygen deaths. Surfacing starts late (oxygen<40), and the climb is vetoed by direction-blind danger flags in the row above.
Removing sticky actions doubles the score to 113.3. Adding a 2-row veto alone raises it to 73.2 on the same 200 seeds. So the score sits near 50 because of one unchecked environment effect, not because of weight errors.
perAttempt.vs_astra:
The two designs are structurally very close:
- Both stay in a fixed column facing left. Astra stays at its start column 5 (100% of steps); Claude homes to column 8.
- Both use row-gated fire/up/down units with diver attraction and a one-row-ahead danger check.
- Both surface on a gauge test.

The differences:
- Astra surfaces at oxygen<60 with any diver (its unit 24 is +1 at oxygen 59 for d≥1); Claude waits for oxygen<40.
- Astra's diver attraction ignores direction (it goes down even for a diver about to leave); Claude's uses the trail channel.
- Astra adds a shooting-opportunity term for enemies in cols 0-3.
- Astra's logits are soft (fire 0.76, up/down about 0.12 each in an empty row); Claude's are nearly deterministic.

Both suffer the sticky double-move failure about equally. For Astra, 127 of 200 deaths were sticky-forced moves into visible danger, and its no-sticky score is 106.5 against 113.3 for Claude.

Measured over 200 episodes each:
- Claude has more oxygen deaths (35 vs 5) and fewer fish deaths (75 vs 104).
- Claude kills more per step (3.70 vs 3.33 per 100 steps) but lives shorter (1,241 vs 1,432 steps).
- Claude rescues fewer divers (22.4 vs 30.0) and earns less bonus (3.88 vs 5.99).

The 1,000-episode gap (51.7 vs 53.1) is about 0.7 standard errors of the difference, assuming Astra's SE is about 1.3, as its 200-episode SE of 2.99 implies. It is not significant. Claude's late, often-vetoed surfacing costs it lifetime, and its higher kill rate makes up for it.

syntheses.headline: Claude's three one-shot Seaquest networks scored 7.41, 7.45 and 51.69 (1,000 episodes each). For reference: zero-weight floor 0.1, PPO 100M 5.6, PPO 500M 88.9, Astra (GPT-6) 53.1. Attempt 3 parks at column 8 facing left and moves only up and down, which is the same plan as Astra's net. It survives about 1,240 steps and finishes 1.4 points behind Astra, a gap that is not statistically significant (z about 0.74). All three beat PPO 100M; none reaches PPO 500M.
syntheses.why_attempts_differ:
The weights are not the problem. Each net.npz is exactly its reply's edits block (228, 204 and 175 statements, max diff 0.0), and both checkers confirmed this for every attempt. The score gap comes from the design each reply chose.

Same-seed rollouts (my rollouts.py, seeds 0-199; the replica matches wsp.play_episode on seeds 0-2):
- Attempt 1: mean 8.03, mean length 350.5 steps. Left/right executed 13.06 times per episode. The sub's front is at column 5 or 6 on 90.6% of steps in rows 1 and below.
- Attempt 2: mean 8.34, length 302.4. Left/right executed 37.45 times per episode (12.4% of steps). Columns 4-5 on 83.4% of steps.
- Attempt 3: mean 49.84, length 1,240.5. Left/right executed 5.74 times per episode (0.46% of steps). Column 8 on at least 99.95% of steps in rows 1-8.

**Attempts 1 and 2 are turrets.**
- Attempt 1's reply says: "The submarine stays parked in columns 5–6. It never steers horizontally except to turn" (answer.md line 5).
- Attempt 2's reply says: "The sub keeps near the centre columns (4–5)... turns to face an enemy in its own row, and fires" (line 5).

Both read facing and target side through linear windows fixed to absolute columns. Those windows share input channels with enemy trails and divers. Both designs also depend on this horizontal logic: masking left/right in memory drops attempt 1 from 8.03 to 2.36 and attempt 2 from 8.34 to 3.98 (my mask_lr.py). So neither can be turned into a fixed-column design by deleting the turns.

Attempt 1's verified failures:
1. The surfacing climb has no hazard term. In 66 of 200 deaths the policy chose up during a surfacing request and hit an enemy, the largest single death class. An oracle that replaces those climbs with fire scores 10.93 against 8.03.
2. The turn detector reads foreign trails as the sub's own back cell. A lone trail at column 7 gives right with p=1.0. Removing foreign trails switches the turn unit off in 206 of 415 turn-driven shifts.
3. The turn detector also counts divers. In 342 of 349 missed turns a diver was on the facing side, and removing the divers fixes 336 of them. But zeroing divers in the turn sum scored 7.06 against 8.03, so no single fix rescues the design.

Attempt 2's verified failures:
1. The facing unit O is correct only when the sub occupies cells (3,4), (4,5) or (5,6). One column further out its sign inverts, and beyond that it reads 0.
2. The side term D steers toward divers. 645 of 763 exits from the central window were diver steps.
3. The step units then walk into enemies, causing 51 of 181 collisions.
4. Off-centre steps were 8.0% of play but carried 88 of 181 collisions (1.825 vs 0.167 per 100 steps).

Fixing these in memory helps but stays far below attempt 3: no diver steering 14.16, true facing 11.14, both 20.31, plus a true bullet detector 21.86.

**Attempt 3 uses a fixed column.** Its reply says: "The submarine parks at column 8, facing left, and fires along its row. It moves only up and down" (line 3). Line 6 adds: "Every threat to a sub at column 8 shows up in columns 6–9 of its row. That makes danger checks fixed cell lookups." With the sub pinned, every column-specific weight stays aligned with its true position, so the absolute-column failures above cannot happen. It also kills faster: 3.705 per 100 steps, against 2.09 for attempt 1.

Its remaining losses:
- **Sticky double moves.** Its vetoes check only the adjacent row. In 200 episodes there were 1,999 sticky-forced row changes; 132 were fatal, 129 of them into a row whose columns 6-9 already showed danger. Adding a 2-row veto raises the score to 73.18 (from 49.84), and turning sticky actions off gives 113.26.
- **Late, direction-blind surfacing.** 35 of 200 episodes end in oxygen deaths, 27 of them with divers aboard. Pooled over those 27 episodes, the climb was vetoed on 901 of 1,032 final surfacing-window steps.

In short, the 7× gap is about survival. The turrets die every 300 steps or so because their horizontal logic misfires. Attempt 3 never relies on horizontal logic after the initial homing.
syntheses.vs_astra:
Astra's published score is 53.11 (se 1.357, 1,000 episodes). The same net scores 54.618 (se 1.352) in the local harness.

**Attempt 3 vs Astra: the same plan in a different column.**
- Astra never samples left or right, and its sub sat at column 5 facing left on all 286,353 steps of 200 episodes (attempt-2 checkers). Attempt 3 sits at column 8 facing left.
- The 1,000-episode gap is 51.69 vs 53.11, or 1.42 points, z 0.74. Against the local 54.618 the z is 1.53. Neither is significant.
- Attempt 3 kills faster: 3.705 vs 3.333 per 100 steps (bootstrap 95% CI of the difference [0.237, 0.511]).
- It lives shorter: 1,240.5 vs 1,431.8 steps on seeds 0-199.
- It has more oxygen deaths: 35 vs 5 per 200 episodes. One verified reason is that it surfaces later. My surf_threshold.py: attempt 3 with 1-3 divers gives p(up)=1.00 at oxygen 39 and 0.00 at 41, while Astra goes up at 59 (1.00) and drops to its 0.12 baseline at 61, for any diver count. The other reason is that attempt 3's climb is blocked by danger flags that ignore direction: in 645 to 682 of 1,233 vetoed surfacing steps, every blocker was moving away from the sub.
- Both nets lose about half their score to sticky actions. With sticky off: attempt 3 113.26, Astra 106.46.

**Attempts 1-2 vs Astra: the gap is mostly survival.**
- Episode lengths are 1,431.8 for Astra against 350.5 and 302.4.
- Attempt 2's policy-caused collision hazard is 0.250 per 100 steps against Astra's 0.019 (13×). The sticky-caused hazard is about the same (0.050 vs 0.047).
- Astra also scores faster overall: 0.0375 vs 0.0276 points per step against attempt 2, and 3.33 vs 2.09 kills per 100 steps against attempt 1.
- In the first 300 steps the rates are close: 0.0261 (attempt 2) vs 0.0241 (Astra) points per step, and 2.07 (attempt 1) vs 2.29 (Astra) kills per 100. So most of Astra's rate advantage comes from later phases that the turrets never reach.
- One checker split the 45.7-point gap between attempt 1 and Astra as about 64% episode length, 24% kill rate and 12% six-diver bonus.

Astra never moves horizontally and dodges vertically instead. A threat within about 2 columns on its right, or a bullet in its row, gives up/down 0.50/0.50. A fish on its left gives fire 1.00.

[0:15] **Output.** Fire has bias 10. Each layer-2 move unit adds +20 to its action when on; the horizontal relays add +22. In an empty row the logits are up 2.3, down 2.4, fire 10, so fire wins at 0.999. In play, fire is 81% of sampled actions.

[0:25] **Homing.** Units HR (27) and HL (28) feed the left/right relays, and Down_0 handles the dive.
- Start at row 0, column 5: HR switches on, right p=1.000.
- Overshoot to column 9 facing right: HL switches on, left p=1.000.
- At column 8 facing left: Down_0, down p=1.000.
- With a fish at row 1, column 7: the row-1 danger flag U1 vetoes the dive, fire p=1.000.
- Result: over 200 episodes the sub is at column 8 on at least 99.95% of steps in rows 1-8.

[0:40] **Which row am I in?** Units S_r (0-8) put weight 6 on each player cell with bias −6, so only the sub's own row reads +1. Each Up_r/Down_r unit gets +100 from its row's S_r, so only the current row's pair can act.

[0:50] **What's worth chasing?** Units R_r (9-16) weight the reward channel by 7.5+4.5·col and the trail channel by −4.5·col, with bias −4.5. That makes direction matter. Measured pre-activations: approaching diver +7.5, receding diver −1.5, approaching fish +10.5.
- A diver approaching in row 6: down 1.000.
- The same diver receding: fire 0.997.
- A diver approaching in row 2: up 1.000.
- A target in the sub's own row cancels the move. A fish in row 4 at column 3 gives fire 1.000: stay and shoot.

[1:10] **What's dangerous?** Units U_r (17-24) flag any danger cell in columns 6-9 of a row.
- Danger in the sub's own row adds +50 to both up and down, so the sub leaves the row 50/50. A fish behind at column 9, or a bullet at column 6, gives up 0.500 / down 0.500.
- Danger in a neighbouring row is a −150 veto. A diver in row 3 plus a fish at row 3, column 7 gives fire 1.000.

[1:25] **Oxygen.** Units HD (25) and SURF (26) and the layer-2 BLOCK unit. SURF reads only gauge cells. It is on with 1-5 divers below oxygen 40, and with 6 divers below 60; both checkers confirmed this by sweeping every oxygen level and diver count.
- Oxygen 30, 2 divers: up 1.000.
- Oxygen 45, 2 divers: fire 0.999.
- 6 divers, oxygen 50: up 1.000.
- A fish moving away at row 3, column 6 still vetoes the climb (fire 1.000). This direction-blind veto is the cause of the oxygen deaths.
- BLOCK stops a surfacing from row 1 without a confirmed diver: the up logit drops to −20 and fire wins at 0.999.

[1:40] **The flaw.** Vetoes look only one row ahead. With a diver approaching in row 3 and a fish at row 2, column 7, U2 is on but Up_4 never reads it, so the sub goes up with p=1.000. A 10% sticky repeat of that move then carries it into row 2.
- Over 200 episodes there were 1,999 sticky-forced row changes; 132 were fatal, and 129 of those went into a row that already showed danger in columns 6-9.
- Adding the missing 2-row veto in memory raises the score to 73.18, against 49.84. Turning sticky actions off gives 113.26.
- The reply's reasoning ends on exactly this gap: "after a dive from row 0, the down move could carry the sub into row 2 without rechecking that row, which is a small gap I'm weighing."

A1: 'Left/right presses cause 83 of 200 deaths'. Refuted by the text checker as an association, not a cause. A2 BUG: 'the reply states flatly that O = 2·(front − back) and the off-window failure is not acknowledged'. Refuted by the text checker: the reply names the cols 3-6 window, and thinking.md lines 465 and 541 acknowledge the off-window risk. A2 BUG: 'the V encoding... can stop the surfacing ascent until oxygen runs out'. Refuted by the text checker. A3: '66% of deaths (132 of 200) were sticky-forced vertical moves into a row whose cols 6-9 already held visible danger'. Refuted by both checkers: 132 deaths followed sticky-forced row changes, but only 129 went into visible danger. The other 3 were sticky ups into row 0 with no diver aboard. I use 132 fatal and 129 into danger, as stated in the unrefuted design-gap claim.

A3 BUG: 'R_r values differ from the reply's +1.5/−1.5 although every sign is right'. Refuted by the text checker. A receding diver at col 8 scores +39.0, approaching fish at cols 6-7 score −1.5, and receding fish at cols 6-7 score −10.5. Only the measured interior values I probed myself (+7.5, −1.5, +10.5) are used.
